terminologyProfile.descriptionRule: Use measurable 3D graphics terms. Avoid vague words unless they are paired with concrete geometry/material/shader parameters.

referenceCamera.note: For likeness work, solve the reference camera (forge/stage1_intake/solve_camera_pose.py) so the review render aligns with the photo and the reference can be projected. Confirm by overlay review.

objectClass.primaryType: hannya mask — noh/kagura demon face shell
objectClass.notes: Depicts a face but is an OBJECT: no body, no skeleton, no hair, never deforms. The character track's landmark/anatomy/rig gates do not apply. Reference is an untextured clay preview, so it carries geometry evidence only — material evidence is declared not applicable rather than extracted from the clay.

reasoning: Silhouette is broken in three directions by paired appendages (horns laterally and superiorly, ears laterally and posteriorly) — not approximable as one ovoid.

The object is a THIN SHELL, not a solid: the rear view shows a continuous posterior rim and daylight through both the eye and mouth apertures. Wall thickness is a real geometric property, so a solid head would be wrong regardless of silhouette score.
Horns are swept 3D arcs: up and laterally (front), leaning back at the base (profile), tips curving forward (top). A tapered cone would pass a silhouette IoU and still be wrong.
Dentition carries identity: four fangs plus a row of ~6 rectangular incisors. These are a few pixels wide and need the microscope tier, not the 64x64 luma grid.
Occlusion risk is LOW rather than typical — six admitted views resolve the rear, the interior, the horn rake and the jaw underside that a single view would have hidden.

specDepthDecision.rationale: Observed structure, not a domain default: 3 macro assemblies (shell, horn pair, ear pair), 8 meso sub-assemblies, 5 micro feature groups, and one genuine repetition system (the incisor row along the maxillary arc).

detailInventory.note: Enumerate every identity-defining small detail before authoring the spec. Each detail must map to a component.localFeatures entry or material.localOverrides entry, never prose only. Use forge/stage1_intake/build_detail_inventory.py to scan zones.

details.description: Left eye aperture: almond through-cut with raised outer canthus; interior visible — a real cut, not a dark patch.
Right eye aperture — reflection of eye-aperture-l across the median plane.
Mouth aperture: wide through-cut between the lips, corners raised; daylight visible through it from the rear view.
Two nostril cavities on the nose underside, flared laterally; confirmed from the below view.
Hard creases bounding the flat faceted plane between the brows; light breaks across real edges, not a normal map.
Brow crest ridgelines rising laterally into the angry V; positive relief catching a highlight on the crest.
Raised collar ring where each horn seats into the cranium — a socket seam, not a butt joint.
Row of ~6 rectangular incisors recessed behind the upper fang line — repeated small parts, an instanced system along the maxillary arc, never one-off meshes.
Paired folds from the alae to the mouth corners; positive relief with shadowed crevices medially.
Cheekbone planes meeting at hard creases — faceted, geometric transitions over the organic base.
Helix/antihelix/concha relief inside each pointed ear; raised curved features, not flat tabs. Better evidence in the profile view.
Continuous wall-thickness rim terminating the shell: cranium apex, behind the ear, around the jaw. Primary evidence is the rear view.

anatomy.note: Only meaningful when objectClass.primaryDomain is character or hybrid. Set applies=true and fill from forge/stage1_intake/extract_landmarks.py. See grimoire/character/reconstruction.md and grimoire/character/likeness_maximization.md.

resolvedUnknowns: wall-thickness [uncertain]: readable only at the rim (rear view), est 0.03-0.05 of head width +/-50% -> adopt 0.05 as a declared parameter; does not affect silhouette gates
interior-relief-depth [uncertain]: rear view shows a soft inverse of the face; depth unmeasurable -> model interior as inner-offset ellipsoid, declared approximation
rim-fillet [uncertain]: sub-pixel -> treat as hard edge, stated stylization
real-world-scale [undetermined]: no scale cue -> author in head-width units; consumer re-normalises to ~1 unit
finish [undetermined]: achromatic clay preview carries no finish evidence; tonal variation is lighting -> materials declared, not extracted; consumer overrides them
incisor-lateral-extent [occluded]: fangs occlude the row's lateral end in every view -> terminate at fang line, declared inference

definitionOfDone: The rendered model matches the reference silhouette, primary proportions, visible component hierarchy, material response, and most recognizable local features for the selected fidelity tier.

featureGroups.name: Horn pair — swept 3D arc
qualityCriteria: Each horn is a swept tube along a 3D curve with monotonic taper to a point, NOT a cone.
Front view: rises and splays laterally. Profile: base leans posteriorly. Top: tip curves anteriorly.
Tip-to-tip span ~1.85x head width; tips rise ~0.24x head width above the cranium apex.
The pair is a reflection across the median plane, with triangle winding flipped.
failureModes: horn built as a straight tapered cone (passes silhouette IoU, fails the arc gate)
horn base butt-joined to the skull instead of seated in its raised collar
pair produced by rotation instead of reflection

featureGroups.name: Hollow shell with through-cut apertures
qualityCriteria: A thin wall with a continuous posterior rim from cranium apex, behind the ear, around the jaw.
Eye and mouth apertures are cut THROUGH the wall — visible as daylight from the rear azimuth.
Interior is concave everywhere; no solid volume behind the face.
failureModes: a solid head that looks correct from the front and has no interior
apertures modelled as dark-painted recesses instead of through-cuts
rim terminating in an open boundary edge loop instead of a closed wall

featureGroups.name: Mouth aperture, four fangs, incisor row
qualityCriteria: Two upper fangs descend and two lower fangs ascend at the aperture corners.
A row of ~6 rectangular incisors sits recessed behind the upper fang line.
Aperture width ~0.46x head width; the row is a repetition system, not modelled one-by-one.
failureModes: fangs omitted or fused into the lip mass
incisor row absent — the single clearest identity marker after the horns
colour-gating the aperture, which is concave and reads cavity shading not material

featureGroups.name: Faceted brow V over almond apertures
qualityCriteria: Brow ridges meet in a hard V with a flat faceted plane between them.
Eye apertures are almond with the outer canthus raised; the ridge overhangs them superiorly.
Creases are geometric (plane meets plane), never a normal-map substitute.
failureModes: brow smoothed into the cranium, losing the faceting that defines the expression
eye apertures round instead of almond, or level instead of canted

featureGroups.name: Pointed lateral ears
qualityCriteria: Pointed, elf-like, embedded in the lateral wall posterior to the horn base, raked posteriorly.
Carry concha/helix relief, not flat tabs.
failureModes: ears omitted entirely (they were missed in the earlier hand-built attempt)
ears as flat extruded tabs with no concha

featureGroups.name: Cheekbone facets and nasolabial folds
qualityCriteria: Cheekbones are faceted planes meeting at creases; nasolabial folds run from the alae to the mouth corners.
failureModes: cheeks smoothed to a generic ovoid, flattening the expression

featureGroups.name: Nose wedge, bridge crease, nostrils
qualityCriteria: A wedge projecting anteriorly with a bridge crease continuing from the brow V; two nostril cavities on the underside.
failureModes: nose bridge rounded instead of creased

featureGroups.name: Measured proportions
qualityCriteria: Shell height 1.51, horn span 1.85, horn rise 0.24, mouth width 0.46 — all normalised to head width 1.00.
failureModes: proportions guessed rather than measured off the reference

visualAcceptance.scoringRule: AI vision must inspect a side-by-side reference/render sheet and score the current pass from 0 to 1. Pixel-diff code may assist diagnostics but cannot approve a pass.

featureReviewPolicy.selectionRule: Choose only the most visually salient, identity-defining, user-prioritized, or high-risk semantic systems. Group repeated parts instead of reviewing every mesh. AI vision scores every selected feature from the same full reference/render pair.

screenshotPolicy.minimumEvidence: Each visual pass needs a reference image, rendered screenshot, side-by-side comparison sheet, AI vision score, layer scores, and critique before choosing continue.
screenshotPolicy.reviewPairRule: Compare the same camera/viewpoint whenever possible; do not judge a front reference against a random render angle.
screenshotPolicy.acceptanceAuthority: AI vision review of the comparison sheet. Code-generated pixel similarity is not sufficient evidence.

referencePbrExtraction.acceptedLimitation: single-image extraction is reference-derived inference, not exact photogrammetry

mustAvoid: plastic-looking smooth bark, stone, cloth, foliage, or aged material

screenshotReview: Compare albedo palette and local color zones.
Compare cavity dirt, edge wear, stains, moss, scratches, or other local masks.
Compare key/fill/rim structure, exposure, tone mapping, background, and contact shadows.
Capture a neutral-light render to verify material readability without reference lighting.
Capture a grazing-light close-up to expose flat normals, uniform roughness, tiling, and plastic highlights.
Capture a reference-matched render from the same camera framing as the source.

actionReadiness.contract: Every macro/meso component should be generated as a stable named Object3D pivot node with a mesh child, action metadata, optional sockets, collider proxy, and destruction metadata.
requiredComponentFields: attachment for child appendages, connectors, limbs, tubes, handles, legs, horns, wings, branches, or cables
authoringRules: Do not collapse independently movable parts into one mesh.
Put transforms on component pivot groups, not only on raw meshes.
For attached child parts, put the pivot at the semantic root/socket and build visible geometry from localStart to localEnd.
Represent hinge, socket, detachable, and breakable intent even when no animation is implemented yet.
Use simplified collider proxies for runtime physics instead of visual mesh colliders by default.

destructionPolicy.fractureGroupNaming: Use stable semantic names such as body-shell, left-hinge, glass-panel, branch-segment.
destructionPolicy.debrisStrategy: Prefer detachable component groups and a small number of procedural fragments over random mesh explosion.

coordinateFrame.front: +Z is anterior (toward the viewer in refs/views/front.png)
coordinateFrame.handedness: right-handed; +X is the mask's own left (image-right in the front view)
coordinateFrame.chirality: every -l/-r pair is a reflection: positions negate x, rotations negate ry and rz, extrude profiles negate profile-x; never a rotation
coordinateFrame.scaleReference: Fitted against measured reference silhouettes, not authored: skull half-width 0.431, horn tip (0.901, 0.983), horn base radius 0.196 taper 0.99 flatten 0.50. Front IoU 0.900, top 0.852, horn-only band 0.855.

negativeSpaces: under the jaw posterior to the chin

componentTree.name: Hollow face shell
componentTree.topologyRationale: Hollow shell whose OUTER envelope is fitted to the reference silhouettes (front IoU 0.900, top 0.852) rather than authored by eye; inner offset gives the wall, eye and mouth apertures are subtracted through it at measured positions.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: A thin conforming shell — front half of a head, open posteriorly — built as an implicit field: outer egg (cranium+jaw+brow bulk) minus an inset inner egg gives the wall; eye and mouth apertures are subtracted THROUGH the wall so daylight passes (rear view evidence).

reviewHistory.summary: Blockout v1: hollow shell + apertures + all 23 parts build and orbit as real volume (multi-angle ok, turntable covered w/ apertures as intended holes). Tier1 FAIL (IoU 0.716, aspect 0.089). Root cause is systematic: face features authored for a shell front at z~0.30 while the built browBulk carries the front to z~0.40-0.46 — brows/glabella/cheeks/lips/nose bridge submerged. Horns under-curved and rooted too low; ears undersized. Self-intersection after real-normals fix: 27/4435 (incisor comb 20 — rebuild; rest is cut-rim noise).
codeFixes: raise+curve horn stations (lateral 0.73->0.80, tips up, base y 0.40->0.50)
push all face features anterior (+0.10..0.14 z) or thin browBulk rz
enlarge ears x1.6 and move anterior

reviewHistory.summary: Blockout v2: face systems recovered (wide canted eye cuts, brow V, nose, ears, dentition all read). Tier1 still FAIL and worse on silhouette (IoU 0.665, aspect 0.118): horn arc bows DOWNWARD (buffalo) instead of steep-at-base concave-down oni arc, dominating silhouette error; cheek plates jut past the face edge as detached slabs; collar rings submerged inside the skull (moved to surface exit point next); gate now also demands a map-stripped render which the harness lacks.
codeFixes: horn stations resampled to slope 1.5->0.2 concave-down profile
cheeks inboard z0.26 rotY0.35 depth0.06 profile x0.8

reviewHistory.summary: Blockout final: Tier1 IoU climbed 0.656->0.716->0.737 across corrections but plateaued below the 0.85 threshold; per the bounded-correction contract a plateau is a stop signal. All structural gates pass: multi-angle non-degenerate, turntable covered with apertures as intended holes, self-intersection 22/4911 (incisor comb gaps + cut-rim noise at res 64), part coverage 22/23 pass. The mask is unmistakably a horned hannya (feature scores 0.55-0.85) at deliberately-primitive blockout fidelity, which matches the stated goal ('примитивную, но узнаваемую'). Decision put to the user: accept blockout fidelity for the fire sandbox (its materials are replaced and the silhouette is what burns), or authorize further correction rounds toward the 0.85 silhouette bar.

reviewHistory.summary: Blockout PASSES after rebuilding by measurement instead of by eye. Silhouette masks extracted from the admitted reference views; envelope parameters fitted with forge/stage4_review/fit_params.fit() rather than authored. Three real bugs found en route: (1) the objective was handed 1-score while fit() MAXIMISES, so it was optimising the error; (2) the horn-only scoring band initially included the skull crown, letting the optimiser buy a better head by deleting the horns; (3) the harness ran at a collapsed viewport, poisoning scale and aspect all along. Tier 1 now PASSES with zero failures: IoU 0.858 (was 0.737), scale delta 0.000, aspect 0.000, symmetry 0.013. Divine Eye 0.721, no hard-gate failures. Interior difference 0.171 over 15699 cells. swept_arc_gate confirms both horns are real arcs (bend radius 1.248, span 41.2 deg, taper 9x).

performanceBudget.optimizationPolicy: Reach accepted visual fidelity first, then optimize without removing reference-critical geometry or surface layers.

lightingFromPhoto.evidence: soft top-left key: brow and cranium crests brightest, shadows fall under brow and lower lip in front.png
shadows never go black — a high-value neutral fill consistent with a seamless grey studio
faint separation light on the posterior rim and horn backs in the rear/profile views

lightingFromPhoto.toneMapping: ACES filmic at exposure 1.0 (neutral studio; no HDR excursions in a matte clay scene)
lightingFromPhoto.shadows: soft contact shadow under the jaw and horn roots; ambient occlusion in cavities only — no ground plane in the reference (mask floats on seamless grey)

proceduralStrategy: implicit SDF (surface nets) for the organic hollow shell + nose + ears
tapered-sweep for the horn arcs; hard-edged extrudes for the faceted brow/glabella/cheek plates
tubes for lips, posterior rim and nasolabial folds; lathe spikes for fangs; one comb extrude for the incisor row
two flat PBR material layers (clay shell, dentition); no textures — the reference is an untextured clay preview and the consumer replaces materials
no stochastic geometry; every coordinate authored (deterministic by construction)
animationAnchors: root pivot node supports whole-object translation, rotation, scale, and visibility changes
component pivot groups support later local transforms without rebuilding geometry
destructionAnchors: actionProfile.destruction.fractureGroup marks detachable or breakable component sets
component seams and sockets define plausible break points instead of random explosions
risks: Surface-nets resolution 64 quantises the thin wall: wall must stay >= 2 cells (0.023/cell at these bounds) or the shell perforates — wall 0.05-0.06 clears it
Turntable hole detection flags the eye/mouth through-cuts by design — run with --allow-holes and verify the HOLES are the apertures, not defects
Extrude plates intersect the implicit shell deliberately (overlap contact); self-intersection gate runs per-mesh, not across the assembly
